content:
jamie.ops: Heads-up — after the admission-controller rollout we've been seeing sustained head-of-line blocking. A subset of GPU hosts are at ~95% while many are idle, backlog grows and oldest jobs never get admitted. p95 queue_wait_seconds spiked to ~12s during the window. Anyone seen this pattern?

scheduler-bot: deploy: admission-controller v2.8.0 rolled to prod at 1784491000 by ci-cd (canary 3/5).

priya.s: Yep, I started a short trace. Looks like the change to preemption ordering in commit 7a9f2c removed the "age" fallback when lanes are full — so high-priority long-running lanes can block older short jobs in other lanes. Repro steps I ran on staging:
```bash
# create mix of short and long jobs with varying priorities
./tools/sched-repro --short 50 --long 5 --pri-dist "0.7:0.3"
watch -n1 ./tools/sched-stats --json | jq '.lanes | {util,queued}'
```
Config snippet that regressed: 
```yaml
preemption:
  ordering: [priority]   # used to be [priority, age]
  fallback_on_full_lane: false
```

kevin-m: Interesting — on staging flipping fallback_on_full_lane -> true normalized admission. Workaround in prod: toggle SCHED_PREEMPT_FALLBACK=true on controllers and rollout. Short-term we also toggled preemption off to let the old ordering handle fairness.

marco.eng: I dug into the controller logs and found a race where token accounting for continuous-batching left a lane token count stuck at 0, which prevented admission for that lane even though GPU had capacity. Logs: 
```
2026-03-17T03:12:11Z controller[pid=42] INFO claim_token lane=short job=abcd status=ok
2026-03-17T03:12:11Z controller[pid=42] ERROR release_token lane=short job=abcd err=stale-ref (did not increment)
2026-03-17T03:12:12Z controller[pid=42] WARN lane=short tokens=0 queued=74
```
That plus the new ordering means the scheduler prefers longer high-prio lanes and never recovers from the token leak.

olivia: Can we do a quick rollback to 2.7.9 while priya prepares a fix? I'd prefer a short canary rollback rather than toggling flags if it's safer. Either way we need a metric and alert: ratio of idle_gpus / total_gpus < 0.2 while overall utilization variance > 0.6.

priya.s: I'll open a PR this morning with a revert of the ordering change + unit + integration test that reproduces the token-leak case. Also adding an alert for per-lane token drift and per-host imbalance. PR will include rollout plan: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 10m gaps.

jamie.ops: Thanks. I'm going to coordinate an emergency action: @kevin-m please apply the fallback toggle in prod (less blast radius) and then we decide rollback vs patch. I'll post status here. :thumbsup:

kevin-m: Applying fallback toggle now (controllers in prod).
scheduler-bot: action: feature-flag-set SCHED_PREEMPT_FALLBACK=true by kevin-m at 1784509800
scheduler-bot: action: rolling-restart controllers (5 replicas) initiated

kevin-m: Restart done. Observing GPU distribution — imbalance decreasing. I'll keep it under observation for 20m and then escalate to rollback if it doesn't stabilize.

priya.s: Opening PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/admission/merge/1234 (revert + tests + alerts). Added reproducer instructions and a script under dev_tools/sched_repro.

jamie.ops: Perfect. Keep the thread updated. If anyone sees a host with >98% sustained and other hosts <20% for more than 10m ping this thread.

olivia: Filing postmortem template entry and tagging SRE oncall to follow-up on root cause & test coverage.

kevin-m: Currently: hosts evening window normalized from 95%/idle to a 60-70% spread. Will monitor. :white_check_mark:
